==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:uder|la:connectō|tree=1}}
From {{uder|en|la|connecto|connectere|fasten together}}, from {{prefix|la|con-|t1=together|necto|alt2=nectere|t2=bind|nocat=1}}, which is cognate with {{cog|en|knot}} and {{cog|en|knit}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|kə-nĕktʹ}}, {{IPA|en|/kəˈnɛkt/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-connect.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{hyphenation|en|con|nect}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkt|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L84}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|of an object}} To [[join]] (to another object): to [[attach]], or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to another object.
#: {{syn|en|affix|join|put together|unite|Thesaurus:join}}
#: {{ant|en|disconnect}}
#: {{ux|en|I think this piece '''connects''' to that piece over there.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|of two objects}} To [[join]]: to [[attach]], or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to each other.
#: {{ux|en|Both roads have the same name, but they don't '''connect''': they're on opposite sides of the river, and there's no bridge there.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|of a blow}} To arrive at an intended target; to [[land]].
#: {{ux|en|When that roundhouse kick '''connected''' with his temple it sent him flying across the room.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|of an object}} To [[join]] (two other objects), or to [[join]] (one object) to (another object): to be a link between two objects, thereby attaching them to each other.
#: {{ux|en|The new railroad will '''connect''' the northern part of the state to the southern part.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=2|passage=Sunning himself on the board steps, I saw for the first time Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke.{{...}}A silver snaffle on a heavy leather watch guard which '''connected''' the pockets of his corduroy waistcoat, together with a huge gold stirrup in his Ascot tie, sufficiently proclaimed his tastes.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=7|passage=With some of it on the south and more of it on the north of the great main thoroughfare that '''connects''' Aldgate and the East India Docks, St. Bede's at this period of its history was perhaps the poorest and most miserable parish in the East End of London.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|of a person}} To [[join]] (two other objects), or to [[join]] (one object) to (another object): to take one object and attach it to another.
#: {{ux|en|I '''connected''' the printer to the computer, but I couldn't get it work.}}
# To join an [[electrical]] or [[telephone]] [[line]] to a [[circuit]] or [[network]].
#: {{ux|en|When the technician '''connects''' my house, I'll be able to access the internet.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1978
|author=w:Richard Nixon
|title=RN: the Memoirs of Richard Nixon
|url=https://archive.org/details/rnmemoirsofricha00nixo/
|publisher=Grosset & Dunlap
|ISBN=0-448-14374-7
|LCCN=77-87793
|OCLC=760525066
|OL=7561812M
|page=568
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/rnmemoirsofricha00nixo/page/568/
|text=Later on, when he had loosened up considerably, he told an amusing story that he said took place during a {{w|Sino-Soviet border conflict|Sino-Soviet border flare-up in 1969}}. "We had a hot line between the Soviet Union and ourselves then," he said, "but it had already become cold because the Kremlin never used it. At the time of the Chen Pao border incident, however, Kosygin picked it up and called us. When our operator answered, he said, 'This is Premier Kosygin. I would like to speak to Chairman Mao.' The operator, completely on his own, said, 'You are a revisionist, and therefore I will not '''connect''' you.' So Kosygin said, 'Well, if you will not try to reach the Chairman, will you please connect me with Prime Minister Chou.' But the operator gave the same unauthorized reply and broke the connection."}}
# To [[associate]]; to establish a relation between.
#: {{ux|en|I didn't '''connect''' my lost jewelry with the news of an area cat burglar until the police contacted me.}}
# To make a [[travel]] [[connection]]; to switch from one means of transport to another as part of the same trip.
#: {{ux|en|I'm flying to London where I '''connect''' with a flight heading to Hungary.}}

|passage=My '''connects''' in Chicago are telling me all kinds of things. Nobody knows anything for sure except that Griffith is missing and money is missing.}}

|passage=I called all my '''connects''', but they were completely dry too.}}
